historical_pattern.summary: In double-ratchet implementations, a message header advertising a large message-number forces the receiver to derive and store every skipped message key up to that number. Without a hard bound this is a remote memory/CPU DoS: one small header triggers unbounded key derivation. dycrpt bounds this with DEFAULT_MAX_SKIP; this campaign attacks the bound.
references: Signal double-ratchet: skipped message keys / MAX_SKIP

surface.notes: DEFAULT_MAX_SKIP is threaded through init_alice/init_bob and deserialize (src/engine/mod.rs:391,491,518). The attack crafts a header whose message number exceeds MAX_SKIP and asserts the receiver refuses rather than deriving unboundedly.

invariant: The number of skipped message keys derived from a single received header is bounded by DEFAULT_MAX_SKIP; a header advertising a jump larger than MAX_SKIP is rejected with an error, not serviced by deriving MAX_SKIP+ keys.
attacker_capabilities: can send a well-formed header with an attacker-chosen (large) message number
can repeat this to sustain pressure
prerequisites: the receiver is in a state where it will attempt skip-key derivation

oracle.success_means: harness prints UNBOUNDED_DERIVATION, i.e. the receiver derived > DEFAULT_MAX_SKIP keys or exceeded the memory/time bound before erroring (invariant broken)
oracle.negative_control: a header advertising a jump of exactly MAX_SKIP must still succeed (print BOUNDED_OK); if even a legitimate in-bound skip fails, the run is INDETERMINATE

severity_rationale: A remote, pre-authentication-adjacent memory/CPU amplification from a single small header is a denial-of-service against every device running the library. Severity is High for a real-time voice/messaging context where the receiver is a phone.
